_meta.indication: FABHALTA is indicated for the treatment of adults with paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria (PNH).

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized (8:5), open-label, active-comparator controlled, 24-week study comparing switching to iptacopan vs continuing anti-C5 treatment (eculizumab or ravulizumab).
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with PNH and residual anemia (Hb <10 g/dL) despite a stable anti-C5 regimen (eculizumab or ravulizumab) for at least 6 months.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Two primary endpoints: proportion with sustained increase of ≥ 2 g/dL in hemoglobin from baseline, and proportion with sustained hemoglobin ≥ 12 g/dL, both in the absence of transfusions.
pivotal_trials.result: Iptacopan response rate 82.3% vs 0% (adjusted difference 81.5%; 95% CI 71.6, 91.4; p<0.0001) for ≥ 2 g/dL Hb increase; transfusion avoidance 95.2% vs 45.7% (difference 49.5%; p<0.0001); Hb change from baseline 3.6 vs -0.1 g/dL.

pivotal_trials.design: Single-arm, open-label 24-week study; all patients received iptacopan 200 mg orally twice daily.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with PNH naive to complement inhibitor therapy, with anemia (Hb <10 g/dL) and LDH >1.5 x ULN.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of patients achieving sustained increase in hemoglobin ≥ 2 g/dL from baseline in the absence of RBC transfusions.
pivotal_trials.result: 77.5% (31/40; 95% CI 61.5, 89.2) achieved sustained Hb increase ≥ 2 g/dL from baseline without RBC transfusions.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥ 10%): headache, nasopharyngitis, diarrhea, abdominal pain, bacterial infection, viral infection, nausea and rash. Serious adverse reactions in 4.8% in APPLY-PNH (pyelonephritis, urinary tract infection, COVID-19) and 5% in APPOINT-PNH (COVID-19, bacterial pneumonia). Serious infections due to encapsulated organisms and elevations in lipids (LDL and triglycerides) were reported.
target_moa: Iptacopan is a complement Factor B inhibitor that binds Factor B of the alternative complement pathway and regulates cleavage of C3, generation of downstream effectors, and amplification of the terminal pathway; it selectively inhibits the alternative pathway.
modality: Small molecule (oral complement Factor B inhibitor)

boxed_warning.content: Boxed warning: Serious infections caused by encapsulated bacteria. FABHALTA increases the risk of serious and life-threatening infections caused by encapsulated bacteria including Streptococcus pneumoniae, Neisseria meningitidis, and Haemophilus influenzae type B; vaccination is required at least 2 weeks prior to the first dose.

rems.type: FABHALTA is available only through a restricted program under a REMS called FABHALTA REMS, to mitigate the risk of serious infections caused by encapsulated bacteria.

advisory_committee.vote: An advisory committee meeting was not convened to discuss this application; no issues were identified that would have benefitted from public discussion with external experts.

summary.text: Iptacopan was reviewed under the 505(b)(1) pathway as a priority review NDA, and had orphan drug designation (granted July 31, 2020) and breakthrough therapy designation (granted December 1, 2020) for PNH. It was a full (not accelerated) approval; postmarketing requirements include a long-term safety registry and completion of the APPLY-PNH and APPOINT-PNH trials.

citations.quote: The Applicant, Novartis Pharmaceutical Corp., seeks approval of iptacopan under the 505(b)(1) regulatory pathway for the treatment of adults with paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria (PNH). Iptacopan is an oral complement inhibitor that targets factor B (FB) to selectively inhibit the alternative pathway, resulting in hematologic response and transfusion avoidance (TA).
